RUN cd /app \
 && sed -i 's|$(LN) -sf ../../$$mod $$target/`basename $$mod`|cp -f $$mod $$target/`basename $$mod`|' Makefile.pre.in \
 && sed -i 's|# create relative links from build/lib\.platform/egg\.so to Modules/egg\.so|# copy build/lib.platform/egg.so from Modules/egg.so (copies, never links: link-bearing trees refuse artifact capture)|' Makefile.pre.in \
 && grep -q 'cp -f \$\$mod' Makefile.pre.in \
 && ! grep -q 'LN) -sf ../../' Makefile.pre.in

# Capped to the task's declared shape (task.toml [environment] cpus = 4):
# an unbounded make reads the host's core count and OOMs under Nest's cap.
# No `|| true`: a failed make must fail the build loudly (mirrors
# environment/Dockerfile).
RUN ./configure -q --prefix=/opt/python-ss007 --with-ensurepip=no \
 && make -j4 -s \
 && rm -rf build/__pycache__ 2>/dev/null \
 && test "$(find build/lib.* -name '*.so' | wc -l)" -gt 50

# Freeze the image's mechanical tree change as one commit (mirrors
# environment/Dockerfile). Tracked-only: build products stay untracked.
RUN cd /app && git add -u \
 && (git diff --cached --quiet || git -c user.name="lambo-task" -c user.email="lambo-task@localhost" commit -qm "task image: frozen build inputs (sharedmods copies)") \
 && test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" \
 && git log --oneline -1

RUN mkdir -p /logs/verifier /tests

COPY . /tests
# GRADING_CONTRACT — ss007-pep752-implicit-namespaces

The graded suite is six conformance files installed at `Lib/test/` by
`test_patch` and run under CPython regrtest (`./python -m test -v ...`)
in the task image. Every id below is the exact `fail_to_pass` string the
parser emits (`test.<module>.<Class>.<method>`); the author must use
these class and method names verbatim.

## Shared rules for every target (read first)

- Imports use only the standard library (`unittest`, `os`, `sys`,
  `json`, `subprocess`, `tempfile`, `contextlib`, `io`, `glob`, `re`,
  `html`, `html.parser`, `argparse`) plus `packagenamespaces`. No
  `test.support`, no third-party packages, no network.
- Guarded import (MANDATORY in every file that touches the package): at
  base the package does not exist, so an unguarded import breaks
  collection and every id goes missing instead of failing. Each such
  file starts with
  `try: from packagenamespaces... import ... except Exception as exc:`
  recording `_IMPORT_ERROR`, and every test that touches the
  implementation calls `self.require_impl()` first, which fails with the
  recorded error. Tests that only use `subprocess` or the filesystem
  need no guard; they fail naturally at base.
- Test methods take no docstrings: regrtest verbose prints a docstring
  instead of the dotted id, and an id-less line can never grade.
- Deterministic only: no randomness, no wall-clock, no absolute paths
  in ids. Temp state goes under `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`.
- The repo root is derived from `__file__` (three levels up from
  `Lib/test/`); never hardcode `/app`.

+"""Grant-management command line for package namespaces (PEP 752).
+
+State lives in a JSON store file (see ``--store``)::
+
+    {"grants": {"acme": "acme-corp"},
+     "projects": {"acme-widget": "acme-corp"},
+     "grandfathered": ["acme-legacy"]}
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+
+from .grants import GrantError, GrantStore, UnknownGrantError
+from .metadata import RepositoryIndex
+from .normalize import normalize_name
+from .uploads import CONFLICT_STATUS, UploadConflictError, authorize_upload
+
+__all__ = ["main", "build_parser"]
+
+#: Exit status when check-upload refuses an upload (a 409 Conflict).
+CONFLICT_EXIT = 3
+
+DEFAULT_STORE = os.path.expanduser("~/.packagenamespaces.json")
+
+
+def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+    """Build the ``packagenamespaces`` argument parser."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        prog="packagenamespaces",
+        description="Manage PEP 752 package-namespace grants.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--store",
+        default=DEFAULT_STORE,
+        help="JSON file holding grants, projects and exemptions "
+        f"(default: {DEFAULT_STORE})",
+    )
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    reserve = sub.add_parser("reserve", help="Reserve a namespace for an owner.")
+    reserve.add_argument("namespace", help="Namespace to reserve.")
+    reserve.add_argument("--owner", required=True, help="Grant owner.")
+
+    sub.add_parser("list", help="List every active grant.").add_argument(
+        "--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON instead of text."
+    )
+
+    show = sub.add_parser("show", help="Show one grant in detail.")
+    show.add_argument("namespace", help="Namespace to show.")
+    show.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON.")
+
+    remove = sub.add_parser("remove", help="Remove a grant.")
+    remove.add_argument("namespace", help="Namespace to release.")
+
+    register = sub.add_parser(
+        "register", help="Record a project's owner."
+    )
+    register.add_argument("project", help="Project name.")
+    register.add_argument("--owner", required=True, help="Project owner.")
+
+    grandfather = sub.add_parser(
+        "grandfather",
+        help="Exempt a pre-existing project from later reservations.",
+    )
+    grandfather.add_argument("project", help="Project name.")
+    grandfather.add_argument("--owner", required=True, help="Project owner.")
+
+    check = sub.add_parser(
+        "check-upload", help="Check whether an upload would be allowed."
+    )
+    check.add_argument("project", help="Project name.")
+    check.add_argument("--owner", required=True, help="Uploading owner.")
+
+    dump = sub.add_parser("dump", help="Dump repository metadata as JSON.")
+    dump.add_argument(
+        "--project",
+        default=None,
+        help="Dump one project-detail mapping instead of the index.",
+    )
+    return parser
+
+
+def _load_index(path: str) -> RepositoryIndex:
+    index = RepositoryIndex(store=GrantStore())
+    try:
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            state = json.load(handle)
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        return index
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        raise GrantError(f"cannot read store {path!r}: {exc}") from exc
+    if not isinstance(state, dict):
+        raise GrantError(f"store {path!r} does not hold a JSON object")
+    grants = state.get("grants", {})
+    if not isinstance(grants, dict):
+        raise GrantError(f"store {path!r} has a non-object 'grants' key")
+    try:
+        for namespace, owner in grants.items():
+            index.store.reserve(namespace, owner)
+    except GrantError:
+        raise
+    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+        raise GrantError(
+            f"store {path!r} holds an invalid grant entry: {exc}"
+        ) from exc
+    projects = state.get("projects", {})
+    if not isinstance(projects, dict):
+        raise GrantError(f"store {path!r} has a non-object 'projects' key")
+    try:
+        for project, owner in projects.items():
+            index.register_project(project, owner)
+    except GrantError:
+        raise
+    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+        raise GrantError(
+            f"store {path!r} holds an invalid project entry: {exc}"
+        ) from exc
+    grandfathered = state.get("grandfathered", [])
+    if not isinstance(grandfathered, list):
+        raise GrantError(
+            f"store {path!r} has a non-array 'grandfathered' key"
+        )
+    try:
+        for project in grandfathered:
+            index.grandfathered.add(project)
+    except GrantError:
+        raise
+    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+        raise GrantError(
+            f"store {path!r} holds an invalid grandfathered entry: {exc}"
+        ) from exc
+    return index
+
+
+def _save_index(path: str, index: RepositoryIndex) -> None:
+    state = {
+        "grants": {
+            name: index.store.get(name).owner
+            for name in index.store.namespaces()
+        },
+        "projects": {
+            project: index.project_owner(project)
+            for project in index.projects()
+        },
+        "grandfathered": index.grandfathered.projects(),
+    }
+    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
+    os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        json.dump(state, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
+        handle.write("\n")
+
+
+def _cmd_reserve(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    grant = index.store.reserve(args.namespace, args.owner)
+    print(f"reserved {grant.name} for {grant.owner}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_list(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    if args.json:
+        print(
+            json.dumps(
+                [
+                    {"name": name, "owner": index.store.get(name).owner}
+                    for name in index.store.namespaces()
+                ]
+            )
+        )
+    else:
+        for name in index.store.namespaces():
+            print(f"{name} {index.store.get(name).owner}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_show(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    detail = index.namespace_detail(args.namespace)
+    if args.json:
+        print(json.dumps(detail, sort_keys=True))
+    else:
+        print(f"name: {detail['name']}")
+        print(f"owner: {detail['owner']}")
+        parent = detail["parent"]
+        print(f"parent: {parent if parent is not None else 'none'}")
+        children = detail["children"]
+        print(f"children: {','.join(children) if children else 'none'}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_remove(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    grant = index.store.remove(args.namespace)
+    print(f"removed {grant.name}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_register(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    index.register_project(args.project, args.owner)
+    print(f"registered {normalize_name(args.project)} for {args.owner}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_grandfather(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    index.register_project(args.project, args.owner)
+    normalized = normalize_name(args.project)
+    index.grandfathered.add(normalized)
+    print(f"grandfathered {normalized}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_check_upload(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    try:
+        authorize_upload(
+            args.project,
+            args.owner,
+            index.store,
+            grandfathered=index.grandfathered,
+        )
+    except UploadConflictError as exc:
+        print(
+            f"{CONFLICT_STATUS} Conflict: project {exc.project!r} matches "
+            f"reserved namespace {exc.namespace!r}",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        return CONFLICT_EXIT
+    print(f"OK {normalize_name(args.project)}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def _cmd_dump(index: RepositoryIndex, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    if args.project is not None:
+        print(json.dumps(index.project_detail(args.project), sort_keys=True))
+    else:
+        print(
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "api_version": index.api_version,
+                    "namespaces": index.list_namespaces(),
+                },
+                sort_keys=True,
+            )
+        )
+    return 0
+
+
+_COMMANDS = {
+    "reserve": (_cmd_reserve, True),
+    "list": (_cmd_list, False),
+    "show": (_cmd_show, False),
+    "remove": (_cmd_remove, True),
+    "register": (_cmd_register, True),
+    "grandfather": (_cmd_grandfather, True),
+    "check-upload": (_cmd_check_upload, False),
+    "dump": (_cmd_dump, False),
+}
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Run the CLI; return the process exit status."""
+    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        index = _load_index(args.store)
+    except GrantError as exc:
+        print(f"packagenamespaces: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    command, persists = _COMMANDS[args.command]
+    try:
+        status = command(index, args)
+    except UnknownGrantError as exc:
+        print(f"packagenamespaces: error: unknown grant: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    except GrantError as exc:
+        print(f"packagenamespaces: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    except (ValueError, UploadConflictError) as exc:
+        print(f"packagenamespaces: error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    if status == 0 and persists:
+        try:
+            _save_index(args.store, index)
+        except OSError as exc:
+            print(
+                f"packagenamespaces: error: cannot write {args.store!r}: {exc}",
+                file=sys.stderr,
+            )
+            return 1
+    return status

+"""Grant lifecycle for package namespaces (PEP 752, Semantics).
+
+A grant reserves a namespace for one owner on one package repository.
+Grants MUST NOT overlap ownership: a proposed namespace that overlaps an
+existing grant held by a different owner is rejected.  Overlap is
+bidirectional -- a longer namespace under an existing grant overlaps just
+as a shorter one over it does -- and is decided by appending a hyphen to
+both normalized names and comparing in both directions, so ``"foo"`` and
+``"foobar"`` never overlap.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import dataclasses
+
+from .matching import namespace_matches
+from .normalize import hyphen_depth, is_valid_namespace, normalize_name
+
+__all__ = [
+    "DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT",
+    "Grant",
+    "GrantError",
+    "InvalidNamespaceError",
+    "OverlapError",
+    "DepthLimitError",
+    "UnknownGrantError",
+    "grants_overlap",
+    "GrantStore",
+]
+
+#: Default cap on the number of hyphens in a granted namespace.  ``None``
+#: disables the limit; repositories SHOULD impose one.
+DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT = 3
+
+
+class GrantError(Exception):
+    """Base class for grant-store errors."""
+
+
+class InvalidNamespaceError(GrantError, ValueError):
+    """A namespace is not a valid project name."""
+
+
+class OverlapError(GrantError):
+    """A proposed namespace overlaps a grant held by another owner."""
+
+
+class DepthLimitError(GrantError):
+    """A proposed namespace exceeds the store's hyphen depth limit."""
+
+
+class UnknownGrantError(GrantError):
+    """No active grant exists for a namespace."""
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class Grant:
+    """A reservation of *name* (normalized) for *owner*."""
+
+    name: str
+    owner: str
+
+
+def grants_overlap(first: str, second: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True if two namespaces overlap.
+
+    Both names are normalized and a hyphen is appended to each before the
+    comparison runs in both directions, so ``"foo"`` overlaps ``"foo-bar"``
+    in either argument order while ``"foo"`` and ``"foobar"`` do not.
+    """
+    first_hyphenated = normalize_name(first) + "-"
+    second_hyphenated = normalize_name(second) + "-"
+    return first_hyphenated.startswith(second_hyphenated) or (
+        second_hyphenated.startswith(first_hyphenated)
+    )
+
+
+def _check_owner(owner: str) -> str:
+    if not isinstance(owner, str) or not owner:
+        raise ValueError("owner must be a non-empty string")
+    return owner
+
+
+class GrantStore:
+    """The active namespace grants of one package repository.
+
+    Grants are per-repository and are never shared between repositories.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, depth_limit: int | None = DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT) -> None:
+        """Create a store; *depth_limit* caps hyphens per namespace.
+
+        ``None`` disables the limit.
+        """
+        self._depth_limit = depth_limit
+        self._grants: dict[str, Grant] = {}
+
+    @property
+    def depth_limit(self) -> int | None:
+        """The configured hyphen depth limit, or None if unlimited."""
+        return self._depth_limit
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._grants)
+
+    def __contains__(self, namespace: object) -> bool:
+        return isinstance(namespace, str) and (
+            normalize_name(namespace) in self._grants
+        )
+
+    def reserve(self, namespace: str, owner: str) -> Grant:
+        """Reserve *namespace* for *owner* and return the new grant.
+
+        The name must be valid and within the depth limit.  A namespace
+        that overlaps an existing grant may only be reserved by that
+        grant's owner; anyone else gets :exc:`OverlapError`.  Reserving
+        the exact same namespace for the same owner is idempotent.
+        """

            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assertIs(is_valid_namespace(name), True)

    def test_invalid_names_reject_non_string(self):
        self.require_impl()
        for value in (["foo"], b"foo", 123, None):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                self.assertIs(is_valid_namespace(value), False)

    def test_valid_names_with_separators(self):
        self.require_impl()
        for name in ("a1.b2_c3-d4", "foo_bar", "foo-bar", "foo.bar"):

                self.assertIs(is_valid_namespace(name), True)

    def test_invalid_names_rejected(self):
        self.require_impl()
        for name in (
            "foo/bar", "foo@bar", "foo bar", "foo!",

            "_foo", "foo_", ".foo", "foo.", "-foo", "foo-",
            ".", "-", "",
        ):
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assertIs(is_valid_namespace(name), False)

    def test_normalize_leaves_clean_names_alone(self):
        self.require_impl()

        self.require_impl()

                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    normalize_name(value)

    def test_normalize_lowercases_and_folds_separators(self):
        self.require_impl()
        cases = (
            ("Foo.Bar_BAZ", "foo-bar-baz"),
            ("foo_bar", "foo-bar"),
            ("Foo", "foo"),
            ("foo.bar", "foo-bar"),
        )
        for name, expected in cases:
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assertEqual(normalize_name(name), expected)

    def test_hyphen_depth_counts(self):
        self.require_impl()
        cases = (
            ("Foo.bar_BAZ", 2),
            ("foo-bar", 1),
            ("foo", 0),
            ("foo-bar-baz", 2),
        )
        for name, expected in cases:
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assertEqual(hyphen_depth(name), expected)

    def test_normalize_collapses_separator_runs(self):
        self.require_impl()
        for name in ("foo___bar", "foo...bar", "foo._-bar", "foo---bar"):
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assertEqual(normalize_name(name), "foo-bar")

class AnchorParser(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.anchors = []
        self._depth = 0
        self._href = None
        self._text = []

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag.lower() == "a":
            if self._depth == 0:
                self._href = dict(
                    (name.lower(), value) for name, value in attrs
                ).get("href")
                self._text = []
            self._depth += 1

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self._depth:
            self._text.append(data)

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag.lower() == "a" and self._depth:
            self._depth -= 1
            if self._depth == 0:
                self.anchors.append((self._href, "".join(self._text)))

    def make_index(self):

        for project, owner in (
            ("acme-widget", "acme-corp"),

            SecurityPolicy(["-bad"], "acme-corp")

        self.assertEqual(policy.owner, "acme-corp")

    def test_evaluate_empty_requirements(self):

class AnchorParser(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.anchors = []
        self._depth = 0
        self._href = None
        self._text = []

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag.lower() == "a":
            if self._depth == 0:
                self._href = dict(
                    (name.lower(), value) for name, value in attrs
                ).get("href")
                self._text = []
            self._depth += 1

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self._depth:
            self._text.append(data)

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag.lower() == "a" and self._depth:
            self._depth -= 1
            if self._depth == 0:
                self.anchors.append((self._href, "".join(self._text)))

class PolicyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def require_impl(self):
        if _IMPORT_ERROR is not None:
            self.fail(f"Cannot exercise namespace policies: {_IMPORT_ERROR!r}")

    def make_index(self):
        store = GrantStore()
        store.reserve("acme", "acme-corp")
        index = RepositoryIndex(store)
        for project, owner in (
            ("acme-widget", "acme-corp"),
            ("acme-legacy", "mallory"),
            ("requests", "psf"),
        ):
            index.register_project(project, owner)
        return index

    def test_policy_validates_owner(self):
        self.require_impl()
        for owner in ("", None, 123):
            with self.subTest(owner=owner):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    SecurityPolicy(["acme"], owner)

    def test_policy_validates_namespaces(self):
        self.require_impl()
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidNamespaceError):
            SecurityPolicy(["-bad"], "acme-corp")
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["Acme.Widgets"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertEqual(policy.namespaces, ("acme-widgets",))
        self.assertEqual(policy.owner, "acme-corp")

    def test_evaluate_empty_requirements(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertEqual(policy.evaluate([], index), {})

    def test_evaluate_normalizes_names(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertEqual(
            policy.evaluate(["Acme.Widget"], index),
            {"acme-widget": True},
        )

    def test_evaluate_reports_each_requirement(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        requirements = ["acme-widget", "acme-legacy", "requests"]
        self.assertEqual(
            policy.evaluate(requirements, index),
            {"acme-widget": True, "acme-legacy": False, "requests": False},
        )

    def test_grant_not_shared_between_repositories(self):
        self.require_impl()
        granted = self.make_index()
        mirror = RepositoryIndex(GrantStore())
        mirror.register_project("acme-widget", "acme-corp")
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertFalse(policy.allows("acme-widget", mirror))
        self.assertTrue(policy.allows("acme-widget", granted))

    def test_denies_unknown_project(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertFalse(policy.allows("acme-unregistered", index))

    def test_denies_grandfathered_foreign_project(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        index.grandfathered.add("acme-legacy")
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertFalse(policy.allows("acme-legacy", index))

    def test_denies_wrong_owner(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "someone-else")
        self.assertFalse(policy.allows("acme-widget", index))

    def test_denies_ungranted_namespace(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["other"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertFalse(policy.allows("other-thing", index))
        index.register_project("acme-widget-part", "acme-corp")
        nested_policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme-widget"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertFalse(nested_policy.allows("acme-widget-part", index))

    def test_allows_with_multiple_namespaces(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policies = (
            (["other", "acme"], True),
            (["other", "ungranted"], False),
        )
        for namespaces, expected in policies:
            with self.subTest(namespaces=namespaces):
                policy = SecurityPolicy(namespaces, "acme-corp")
                self.assertIs(policy.allows("acme-widget", index), expected)

    def test_allows_granted_owner_dependency(self):
        self.require_impl()
        index = self.make_index()
        policy = SecurityPolicy(["acme"], "acme-corp")
        self.assertTrue(policy.allows("acme-widget", index))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent behavioral probe for the PEP 752 task (second reward channel).

Usage: probe.py <repo-root> <output-json>

Writes ``{"passed": bool, "failed": [...], "checks": N}``. ``passed`` is true
only when every check below holds. Any unexpected error fails closed
(``passed`` is false, never missing).

WHY THIS EXISTS

The graded suite's verdicts travel through the JUnit XML report, which is
written inside the same container -- and the same process -- as agent code:
the agent-owned interpreter runs the regrtest process, and the agent's own
package is imported into it. In-process code can therefore rewrite the
report after a genuine failing run (an atexit hook suffices) and a
report-only grader scores reward 1. This probe closes that route: it
re-checks the specified behaviors directly -- including negative cases --
and NEVER reads the JUnit report. The reward requires this probe AND every
required suite id, so a forged report alone can no longer score.

WHY THREE PROCESSES

An earlier single-process probe imported the submitted package in the same
process that wrote its verdict file, so a shutdown hook inside the package
could overwrite the genuine payload afterwards and the reward accepted the
forgery. Splitting off a verdict-writing parent closed that route but not
the next one: the child still imports agent code to run the checks, and
that code can patch the test framework (``unittest.TestCase.run``) or arm
a ``sys.settrace`` hook that swaps the check functions for no-ops, forging
a passing payload the parent would then faithfully write. A parent that
merely writes what the child computed authenticates nothing.

This probe therefore splits in three. The CHECK CHILD runs in a fresh
locked-down interpreter (absolute repo path, ``-I -S``, neutral cwd,
scrubbed environment, script from the verifier-owned ``/tests`` tree),
imports the implementation under test, runs every check, and prints its
verdict as one marked line on stdout. The ATTEST GRANDCHILD runs the same
locked-down way but NEVER imports agent code: it only hashes the check
functions' bytecode, giving the parent ground truth no submission can
influence. The PARENT never imports agent-controlled code -- it spawns
both, demands exactly one well-formed result line on a zero exit from
each, requires the child's per-check code hashes to equal the
grandchild's (a swapped check has different bytecode, however its
filename was faked), and only then writes the verdict file, after both
(and any hook the child armed) are dead. Anything the child writes to
the verdict path is moot: the parent overwrites it last. Every anomaly
-- crash, timeout, missing or doubled result line, malformed payload,
attestation mismatch -- fails closed.

The probe pins specified behavior only (the same contract the graded suite
is authored from), never reference-implementation internals, so any correct
alternate implementation passes it.
"""

import contextlib
import glob
import hashlib
import io
import json
import marshal
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types
import unittest
from html.parser import HTMLParser

# The child prints its verdict as one line starting with this marker; the
# parent accepts exactly one such line. Genuine implementation code never
# prints it; extra copies fail closed.
MARKER = "LAMBO_PROBE_PAYLOAD "

_MODE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] in (
    "--child", "--attest") else None
_CHILD_MODE = _MODE == "--child"
_ATTEST_MODE = _MODE == "--attest"

if _CHILD_MODE:
    try:
        from packagenamespaces import (
            API_VERSION,
            CONFLICT_EXIT,
            CONFLICT_STATUS,
            DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT,
            LEGACY_API_VERSION,
            GrantStore,
            RepositoryIndex,
            SecurityPolicy,
            UploadConflictError,
            authorize_upload,
            grants_overlap,
            hyphen_depth,
            is_valid_namespace,
            namespace_matches,
            normalize_name,
        )
        from packagenamespaces.cli import main as cli_main
        from packagenamespaces.grants import (
            DepthLimitError,
            InvalidNamespaceError,
            OverlapError,
            UnknownGrantError,
        )
        from packagenamespaces.metadata import NotSupportedError
        from packagenamespaces.uploads import GrandfatheredRegistry
    except Exception as exc:  # Base tree or broken package: fail closed.
        _IMPORT_ERROR = exc
    else:
        _IMPORT_ERROR = None
else:
    # Parent mode: agent-controlled code is never imported here. The check
    # functions below are defined but never called in this process.
    _IMPORT_ERROR = None


if _MODE is not None:
    REPO_ROOT = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "/app"
else:
    REPO_ROOT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/app"
REPO_PYTHON = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "python")
DESTDIR = "/tmp/lambo-destdir"

_FAILURES = []
_ATTEST_PRE = {}
_ATTEST_POST = {}


def _code_hash(func):
    """Bytecode digest identifying the running check function."""
    return hashlib.sha256(func.__code__.co_code).hexdigest()


def check(name, func):
    """Run one check, recording its name on any failure.

    The check's bytecode is hashed immediately before and after it runs.
    The parent compares both against the attestation grandchild's ground
    truth, so a no-op swapped in around the call -- however briefly --
    fails closed even if the swap is undone before the verdict prints.
    """
    try:
        _ATTEST_PRE[name] = _code_hash(func)
    except Exception as exc:
        _FAILURES.append(f"{name}: cannot attest check code: {exc!r}")
        return
    try:
        func()
    except Exception as exc:
        _FAILURES.append(f"{name}: {exc!r}")
    except BaseException as exc:
        # An exiting check (argparse SystemExit, a deliberate os._exit
        # dodge) fails that check; the rest still run.
        _FAILURES.append(f"{name}: {type(exc).__name__}({exc})")
    finally:
        try:
            _ATTEST_POST[name] = _code_hash(func)
        except Exception as exc:
            _FAILURES.append(f"{name}: cannot re-attest check code: {exc!r}")


def need_impl():
    if _IMPORT_ERROR is not None:
        raise AssertionError(f"cannot import packagenamespaces: {_IMPORT_ERROR!r}")


def expect_raises(exc_types, func, *args, **kwargs):
    try:
        func(*args, **kwargs)
    except exc_types:
        return
    raise AssertionError(f"{func.__name__} did not raise {exc_types}")


# ------------------------------------------------------------- integrity
#
# These run first and need no implementation: they verify the child process
# itself has not been tampered with by the submission it imported. A forged
# suite report (patched ``TestCase.run``) or forged probe payload (check
# functions swapped for no-ops under a trace hook) fails here, in a process
# whose own checks are attested by a grandchild that never imports agent
# code. At base, with nothing imported, they pass.

def integrity_no_trace():
    # No trace hook may be active: swapping checks for no-ops needs one.
    trace = sys.gettrace()

def integrity_unittest_run_truthful():
    # Behavior, to say what the identity check means: a failing test
    # fails, a passing test passes, and the test body really executes.
    seen = []

    class _InnerAlpha(unittest.TestCase):
        def runTest(self):
            seen.append("alpha")
            self.fail("inner failure must be reported")

    class _InnerBeta(unittest.TestCase):
        def runTest(self):
            seen.append("beta")

    failing = unittest.TestResult()
    _InnerAlpha().run(failing)
    assert seen == ["alpha"], seen
    assert failing.wasSuccessful() is False
    assert len(failing.failures) == 1
    passing = unittest.TestResult()
    _InnerBeta().run(passing)
    assert seen == ["alpha", "beta"], seen
    assert passing.wasSuccessful() is True

def grants_root_exports():
    # The package root re-exports every public symbol: Grant and GrantError
    # are named in the spec and must resolve from the root (a tree that
    # drops them still passes every other channel, so this check pins
    # them). The import is local so a missing export fails this check,
    # not the whole child. Re-export means identity with the defining
    # submodule's object. `__all__` itself is NOT specified: when absent
    # nothing is pinned, and when present any equivalent spelling -- list
    # or tuple -- passes as long as every entry resolves from the root.
    need_impl()
    import packagenamespaces
    from packagenamespaces import Grant, GrantError
    from packagenamespaces import grants as grants_module
    assert issubclass(GrantError, Exception)
    assert packagenamespaces.Grant is grants_module.Grant
    assert packagenamespaces.GrantError is grants_module.GrantError
    declared = getattr(packagenamespaces, "__all__", None)
    if declared is not None:
        assert isinstance(declared, (list, tuple)), type(declared)
        for name in declared:
            assert isinstance(name, str), name
            assert hasattr(packagenamespaces, name), name

def harness_scripts_use_no_network():
    # Behavioral, never textual: no word in either script is matched, so a
    # comment merely mentioning a network tool passes. Instead the scripts
    # run with every network command shadowed by a stub that logs its
    # invocation and fails: genuine shell-outs to the network then fail
    # (the stub's exit 1 under `set -e`, or the empty-log assertion),
    # while offline scripts succeed with zero invocations. Commented
    # copies prove the point directly by still passing.
    network_cmds = ("curl", "wget", "ssh", "scp", "sftp", "ftp", "lftp",
                    "telnet", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "httpx")
    comment = ("# offline by design: curl wget ssh scp sftp ftp lftp "
               "telnet nc ncat socat httpx urllib http.client\n")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        stubdir = os.path.join(tmp, "stubs")
        os.mkdir(stubdir)
        log = os.path.join(tmp, "invocations.log")
        for cmd in network_cmds:
            stub = os.path.join(stubdir, cmd)
            with open(stub, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(f"#!/bin/bash\necho {cmd} >> {log}\nexit 1\n")
            os.chmod(stub, 0o755)
        env = {"PATH": stubdir + os.pathsep + "/usr/bin:/bin",
               "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1"}
        fixtures = os.path.join(tmp, "fixtures")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", _tools_path("gen_fixtures.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", _tools_path("verify_offline.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()
        # Copies carrying network-word comments behave identically. The
        # copies sit in a mirrored Tools/ layout with Lib linked back to
        # the repo, because the verifier derives its root from its own
        # path; only the trailing comment differs from the real scripts.
        mirror = os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Tools", "packagenamespaces")
        os.makedirs(mirror)
        os.symlink(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "Lib"),
                   os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Lib"))
        commented = {}
        for script in ("gen_fixtures.sh", "verify_offline.sh"):
            with open(_tools_path(script), encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                content = handle.read()
            copy_path = os.path.join(mirror, script)
            with open(copy_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(content + comment)
            commented[script] = copy_path
        alt_fixtures = os.path.join(tmp, "alt-fixtures")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["gen_fixtures.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["verify_offline.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()

def _child_main(argv):
    """Run every check and print the verdict as one marked stdout line."""
    if len(argv) != 3:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: probe.py --child <repo-root>\n")
        return 2
    for name, func in CHECKS:
        check(name, func)
    payload = {
        "passed": not _FAILURES,
        "failed": sorted(_FAILURES),
        "checks": len(CHECKS),
        "attest": {"pre": dict(_ATTEST_PRE), "post": dict(_ATTEST_POST)},
    }
    sys.stdout.write(MARKER + json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    if _FAILURES:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"probe: {len(_FAILURES)}/{len(CHECKS)} checks failed\n")
        for failure in sorted(_FAILURES):
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {failure}\n")
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: all {len(CHECKS)} checks passed\n")
    return 0


def _parent_main(argv):
    """Spawn the child, validate its one result line, write the verdict.

    This process never imports agent-controlled code. The verdict file is
    written only here, after the child has exited, so a shutdown hook the
    child armed cannot rewrite it afterwards: anything it wrote is moot.
    A second spawn -- the attestation grandchild, which never imports
    agent code either -- supplies ground-truth check hashes the child's
    per-check digests must equal, so swapped checks fail closed even
    when the child's own verdict claims they passed.
    """
    if len(argv) != 3:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: probe.py <repo-root> <output-json>\n")
        return 2
    repo_root, output_path = argv[1], argv[2]

    def fail_closed(reason):
        payload = {"passed": False, "failed": [reason],
                   "checks": len(CHECKS)}
        try:
            with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
                handle.write("\n")
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: cannot write {output_path}: {exc}\n")
            return 2
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {reason}\n")
        return 0

    def spawn(mode):
        """Run one locked-down grandchild, return its marked payload."""
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [child_bin, "-I", "-S",
                 os.path.abspath(__file__), mode, repo_root],
                capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=900,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True,
                env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1"},
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} process timed out"
        except Exception as exc:  # Missing binary, decode failure, ...
            return None, f"probe: cannot run {mode} process: {exc!r}"
        if proc.stderr:
            sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} process exited {proc.returncode}"
        lines = [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines()
                 if line.startswith(MARKER)]
        if len(lines) != 1:
            return None, (f"probe: {mode} expected 1 result line, "
                          f"saw {len(lines)}")
        try:
            return json.loads(lines[0][len(MARKER):]), None
        except ValueError as exc:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} result line is not JSON: {exc}"

    child_bin = os.path.join(repo_root, "python")
    try:
        with open(child_bin, "rb") as handle:
            magic = handle.read(4)
    except OSError as exc:
        return fail_closed(f"probe: cannot read check interpreter: {exc!r}")
    # Never execute a replacement: only a built ELF executable may run the
    # checks (run_script.sh already relinked a non-ELF binary; anything
    # still wrong here fails closed instead of running it).
    if magic != b"\x7fELF" or not os.access(child_bin, os.X_OK):
        return fail_closed(
            "probe: check interpreter is not a built executable")
    payload, error = spawn("--child")
    if error is not None:
        return fail_closed(error)
    if (not isinstance(payload, dict)
            or payload.get("checks") != len(CHECKS)
            or not isinstance(payload.get("passed"), bool)
            or not isinstance(payload.get("failed"), list)
            or not all(isinstance(entry, str)
                       for entry in payload["failed"])
            or not isinstance(payload.get("attest"), dict)):
        return fail_closed("probe: result line has a bad shape")
    attested, error = spawn("--attest")
    if error is not None:
        return fail_closed(error)
    expected_names = [name for name, _ in CHECKS]
    if (not isinstance(attested, dict)
            or attested.get("names") != expected_names
            or not isinstance(attested.get("hashes"), dict)):
        return fail_closed("probe: attestation has a bad shape")
    truth = attested["hashes"]
    claimed = payload["attest"]
    for side in ("pre", "post"):
        digests = claimed.get(side)
        if not isinstance(digests, dict):
            return fail_closed(
                f"probe: attestation {side} has a bad shape")
        for name in expected_names:
            if digests.get(name) != truth.get(name):
                return fail_closed(
                    f"probe: check code mismatch for {name} ({side})")
    try:
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            handle.write("\n")
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: cannot write {output_path}: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    if payload["passed"]:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: all {len(CHECKS)} checks passed\n")
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"probe: {len(payload['failed'])}/{len(CHECKS)} checks failed\n")
        for failure in sorted(payload["failed"]):
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {failure}\n")
    return 0


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) > 1 and argv[1] == "--child":
        return _child_main(argv)
    if len(argv) > 1 and argv[1] == "--attest":
        return _attest_main(argv)
    return _parent_main(argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        exit_code = main(sys.argv)
    except BaseException as exc:  # Fail closed, always with a payload.
        if _CHILD_MODE or _ATTEST_MODE:
            try:
                if _ATTEST_MODE:
                    failed = {"names": [], "hashes": {}}
                else:
                    failed = {"passed": False, "failed": [f"probe: {exc!r}"],
                              "checks": len(CHECKS),
                              "attest": {"pre": dict(_ATTEST_PRE),
                                         "post": dict(_ATTEST_POST)}}
                sys.stdout.write(MARKER + json.dumps(
                    failed, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
                sys.stdout.flush()
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: fatal: {exc!r}\n")
            exit_code = 0
        else:
            try:
                with open(sys.argv[2], "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                    json.dump({"passed": False,
                               "failed": [f"probe: {exc!r}"],
                               "checks": len(CHECKS)}, handle)
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: fatal: {exc!r}\n")
            exit_code = 0
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def _save(path, index):

class SecurityPolicy:
    """Allow projects owned by owner under its active policy namespaces."""

    def __init__(self, namespaces, owner):
        _validate_owner(owner)
        if isinstance(namespaces, str):
            namespaces = (namespaces,)
        try:
            namespaces = iter(namespaces)
        except TypeError:
            raise InvalidNamespaceError(
                'namespaces must be an iterable of names'

        self._namespaces = tuple(_validate_name(name) for name in namespaces)
        self._owner = owner

    def namespaces(self):
        return self._namespaces

    @property
    def owner(self):
        return self._owner

    def allows(self, project, index):
        """Check project ownership and an active grant on this index."""
        project = normalize_name(project)
        if (not index.supports_namespaces
                or index.project_owner(project) != self.owner):
            return False
        for namespace in self.namespaces:
            grant = index.store.get(namespace)
            if (grant is not None and grant.owner == self.owner
                    and namespace_matches(namespace, project)):
                return True
        return False

    def evaluate(self, requirements, index):
        """Return normalized project names mapped to their policy decisions."""
        return {normalize_name(project): self.allows(project, index)
                for project in requirements}

class UploadConflictError(Exception):
    """An uploader does not own a matching reserved namespace."""

    status_code = CONFLICT_STATUS

class GrandfatheredRegistry:
    """Keep normalized project names exempt from namespace upload checks."""

    def __init__(self, projects=()):
        self._projects = set()
        for project in projects:
            self.add(project)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._projects)

    def __contains__(self, project):
        return (isinstance(project, str)
                and normalize_name(project) in self._projects)

    def add(self, project):
        """Exempt a project from namespace upload checks."""
        self._projects.add(_validate_name(project))

    def discard(self, project):
        """Remove an exemption, if present."""
        self._projects.discard(normalize_name(project))

    def covers(self, project):
        """Return whether the normalized project is exempt."""
        return project in self

    def projects(self):
        """Return exempt project names in sorted order."""
        return sorted(self._projects)


def authorize_upload(project, owner, store, grandfathered=None):
    """Return True when allowed, otherwise raise UploadConflictError.

    Validate the uploader before consulting grants, even for unreserved or
    grandfathered projects.  Exemptions apply to complete project names.
    """
    _validate_owner(owner)
    project = _validate_name(project)
    if grandfathered is not None and grandfathered.covers(project):
        return True
    for grant in store.matching(project):
        if grant.owner != owner:
            raise UploadConflictError(project, grant.name, owner)
    return True

def _child_main(argv):
    """Run every check and print the verdict as one marked stdout line."""
    if len(argv) != 3:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: probe.py --child <repo-root>\n")
        return 2
    for name, func in CHECKS:
        check(name, func)
    payload = {
        "passed": not _FAILURES,
        "failed": sorted(_FAILURES),
        "checks": len(CHECKS),
        "attest": {"pre": dict(_ATTEST_PRE), "post": dict(_ATTEST_POST)},
    }
    sys.stdout.write(MARKER + json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    if _FAILURES:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"probe: {len(_FAILURES)}/{len(CHECKS)} checks failed\n")
        for failure in sorted(_FAILURES):
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {failure}\n")
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: all {len(CHECKS)} checks passed\n")
    return 0


def _parent_main(argv):
    """Spawn the child, validate its one result line, write the verdict.

    This process never imports agent-controlled code. The verdict file is
    written only here, after the child has exited, so a shutdown hook the
    child armed cannot rewrite it afterwards: anything it wrote is moot.
    A second spawn -- the attestation grandchild, which never imports
    agent code either -- supplies ground-truth check hashes the child's
    per-check digests must equal, so swapped checks fail closed even
    when the child's own verdict claims they passed.
    """
    if len(argv) != 3:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: probe.py <repo-root> <output-json>\n")
        return 2
    repo_root, output_path = argv[1], argv[2]

    def fail_closed(reason):
        payload = {"passed": False, "failed": [reason],
                   "checks": len(CHECKS)}
        try:
            with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
                handle.write("\n")
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: cannot write {output_path}: {exc}\n")
            return 2
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {reason}\n")
        return 0

    def spawn(mode):
        """Run one locked-down grandchild, return its marked payload."""
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [child_bin, "-I", "-S",
                 os.path.abspath(__file__), mode, repo_root],
                capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=900,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True,
                env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1"},
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} process timed out"
        except Exception as exc:  # Missing binary, decode failure, ...
            return None, f"probe: cannot run {mode} process: {exc!r}"
        if proc.stderr:
            sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} process exited {proc.returncode}"
        lines = [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines()
                 if line.startswith(MARKER)]
        if len(lines) != 1:
            return None, (f"probe: {mode} expected 1 result line, "
                          f"saw {len(lines)}")
        try:
            return json.loads(lines[0][len(MARKER):]), None
        except ValueError as exc:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} result line is not JSON: {exc}"

    child_bin = os.path.join(repo_root, "python")
    try:
        with open(child_bin, "rb") as handle:
            magic = handle.read(4)
    except OSError as exc:
        return fail_closed(f"probe: cannot read check interpreter: {exc!r}")
    # Never execute a replacement: only a built ELF executable may run the
    # checks (run_script.sh already relinked a non-ELF binary; anything
    # still wrong here fails closed instead of running it).
    if magic != b"\x7fELF" or not os.access(child_bin, os.X_OK):
        return fail_closed(
            "probe: check interpreter is not a built executable")
    payload, error = spawn("--child")
    if error is not None:
        return fail_closed(error)
    if (not isinstance(payload, dict)
            or payload.get("checks") != len(CHECKS)
            or not isinstance(payload.get("passed"), bool)
            or not isinstance(payload.get("failed"), list)
            or not all(isinstance(entry, str)
                       for entry in payload["failed"])
            or not isinstance(payload.get("attest"), dict)):
        return fail_closed("probe: result line has a bad shape")
    attested, error = spawn("--attest")
    if error is not None:
        return fail_closed(error)
    expected_names = [name for name, _ in CHECKS]
    if (not isinstance(attested, dict)
            or attested.get("names") != expected_names
            or not isinstance(attested.get("hashes"), dict)):
        return fail_closed("probe: attestation has a bad shape")
    truth = attested["hashes"]
    claimed = payload["attest"]
    for side in ("pre", "post"):
        digests = claimed.get(side)
        if not isinstance(digests, dict):
            return fail_closed(
                f"probe: attestation {side} has a bad shape")
        for name in expected_names:
            if digests.get(name) != truth.get(name):
                return fail_closed(
                    f"probe: check code mismatch for {name} ({side})")
    try:
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            handle.write("\n")
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: cannot write {output_path}: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    if payload["passed"]:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: all {len(CHECKS)} checks passed\n")
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"probe: {len(payload['failed'])}/{len(CHECKS)} checks failed\n")
        for failure in sorted(payload["failed"]):
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {failure}\n")
    return 0


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) > 1 and argv[1] == "--child":
        return _child_main(argv)
    if len(argv) > 1 and argv[1] == "--attest":
        return _attest_main(argv)
    return _parent_main(argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        exit_code = main(sys.argv)
    except BaseException as exc:  # Fail closed, always with a payload.
        if _CHILD_MODE or _ATTEST_MODE:
            try:
                if _ATTEST_MODE:
                    failed = {"names": [], "hashes": {}}
                else:
                    failed = {"passed": False, "failed": [f"probe: {exc!r}"],
                              "checks": len(CHECKS),
                              "attest": {"pre": dict(_ATTEST_PRE),
                                         "post": dict(_ATTEST_POST)}}
                sys.stdout.write(MARKER + json.dumps(
                    failed, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
                sys.stdout.flush()
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: fatal: {exc!r}\n")
            exit_code = 0
        else:
            try:
                with open(sys.argv[2], "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                    json.dump({"passed": False,
                               "failed": [f"probe: {exc!r}"],
                               "checks": len(CHECKS)}, handle)
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: fatal: {exc!r}\n")
            exit_code = 0
    sys.exit(exit_code)

    local cid="$1" mode="${2:-solve}"

        docker exec "$cid" bash /solution/solve.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    fi

grade_once() {
    # $1=cid; runs test.sh, prints the reward (0.0 on any failure to read).
    local cid="$1" reward
    docker exec "$cid" bash /tests/test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    reward="$(docker exec "$cid" cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0)"

run_control() {
    # $1=kind $2=name $3=mode(nosolve|solve) $4=overlay-dir-or-empty
    local kind="$1" name="$2" mode="$3" overlay="$4" cid reward
    echo "CONTROL-BEGIN $kind $name"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    cid="$(LAMBO_CONTROL="$kind/$name" docker run -d --rm $LIMITS "$IMG" sleep 3600)" || {
        echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=ERROR_NO_CONTAINER"
        return 0
    }
    export LAMBO_CONTROL="$kind/$name"
    if ! stage_and_solve "$cid" "$mode"; then
        echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=ERROR_NO_SOLVE"
        docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -n "$overlay" ]; then
        docker cp "$overlay/." "$cid:/app/" >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
    reward="$(grade_once "$cid")"
    echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=$reward"
    docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1
    unset LAMBO_CONTROL
    return 0
}

run_twice() {
    # $1=unit; grades the solved state twice in one container.
    local unit="$1" cid first second
    echo "CONTROL-BEGIN twice $unit"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    cid="$(LAMBO_CONTROL="twice/$unit" docker run -d --rm $LIMITS "$IMG" sleep 3600)" || {
        echo "CONTROL twice $unit reward=ERROR_NO_CONTAINER"

        return 0

    first="$(grade_once "$cid")"

    echo "CONTROL twice $unit reward=$first,$second"

    unset LAMBO_CONTROL

# Control harness: probe the reward signal with known-good/known-bad trees.

#

#   CONTROL neg <name> reward=<r>   wrong / gaming / no-op
#   CONTROL twice <unit> reward=<a>,<b>  same state graded twice

LIMITS="--cpus=4 --memory=8192m --memory-swap=8192m"

    -t "$IMG" -f "$TASKDIR/environment/Dockerfile" "$TASKDIR/environment" \
    >"$TASKDIR/build/.controls-build.log" 2>&1 || {
    echo "run_controls: image build failed; see build/.controls-build.log" >&2
    exit 1
}

stage_and_solve() {
    # $1=cid; stages /tests and /solution, runs solve.sh unless $2 == nosolve.
    local cid="$1" mode="${2:-solve}"
    docker cp "$TASKDIR/steps/$STEP/tests/." "$cid:/tests/" >/dev/null 2>&1
    if [ "$mode" = solve ]; then
        docker exec "$cid" bash -c 'rm -rf /solution && mkdir -p /solution' >/dev/null 2>&1
        docker cp "$TASKDIR/steps/$STEP/solution/." "$cid:/solution/" >/dev/null 2>&1
        docker exec "$cid" bash /solution/solve.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

grade_once() {
    # $1=cid; runs test.sh, prints the reward (0.0 on any failure to read).
    local cid="$1" reward
    docker exec "$cid" bash /tests/test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    reward="$(docker exec "$cid" cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0)"
    if [ "$reward" = "1" ]; then reward="1.0"; fi
    if [ "$reward" = "0" ]; then reward="0.0"; fi
    printf '%s' "$reward"
}

run_control() {
    # $1=kind $2=name $3=mode(nosolve|solve) $4=overlay-dir-or-empty
    local kind="$1" name="$2" mode="$3" overlay="$4" cid reward
    echo "CONTROL-BEGIN $kind $name"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    cid="$(LAMBO_CONTROL="$kind/$name" docker run -d --rm $LIMITS "$IMG" sleep 3600)" || {
        echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=ERROR_NO_CONTAINER"
        return 0
    }
    export LAMBO_CONTROL="$kind/$name"
    if ! stage_and_solve "$cid" "$mode"; then
        echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=ERROR_NO_SOLVE"
        docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -n "$overlay" ]; then
        docker cp "$overlay/." "$cid:/app/" >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
    reward="$(grade_once "$cid")"
    echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=$reward"
    docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1
    unset LAMBO_CONTROL
    return 0
}

run_twice() {
    # $1=unit; grades the solved state twice in one container.
    local unit="$1" cid first second
    echo "CONTROL-BEGIN twice $unit"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    cid="$(LAMBO_CONTROL="twice/$unit" docker run -d --rm $LIMITS "$IMG" sleep 3600)" || {
        echo "CONTROL twice $unit reward=ERROR_NO_CONTAINER"
        return 0
    }
    export LAMBO_CONTROL="twice/$unit"
    if ! stage_and_solve "$cid" solve; then
        echo "CONTROL twice $unit reward=ERROR_NO_SOLVE"
        docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return 0
    fi
    first="$(grade_once "$cid")"
    second="$(grade_once "$cid")"
    echo "CONTROL twice $unit reward=$first,$second"
    docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1
    unset LAMBO_CONTROL
    return 0
}

    # submodule's object. `__all__` itself is NOT specified: when absent
    # nothing is pinned, and when present any equivalent spelling -- list
    # or tuple -- passes as long as every entry resolves from the root.
    need_impl()

    from packagenamespaces import Grant, GrantError
    from packagenamespaces import grants as grants_module

    assert packagenamespaces.GrantError is grants_module.GrantError

class _AnchorCollector(HTMLParser):
def metadata_html():
    need_impl()
    index = RepositoryIndex()
    files = [
        {"filename": "demo-1.0.tar.gz",
         "url": "https://example.com/demo-1.0.tar.gz"},
        {"filename": "demo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
         "url": "https://example.com/demo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"},
    ]
    page = index.simple_html("demo", files)
    assert index.simple_html("demo", files) == page  # deterministic
    assert "namespace" not in page
    assert re.search(r"(?i)<!doctype\s+html\s*>", page)
    for tag in ("html", "head", "body"):
        assert re.search(rf"(?i)<{tag}\b[^>]*>", page), tag
    # Title and heading name the project; the exact wording is free.
    for tag in ("title", "h1"):
        match = re.search(rf"(?i)<{tag}\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)</{tag}\s*>", page)
        assert match, tag
        assert "demo" in match.group(1), tag
    # One anchor per file, in order; spelling of the markup is free.
    assert _collect_anchors(page) == [
        (entry["url"], entry["filename"]) for entry in files]
    tricky = index.simple_html("demo", [{
        "filename": 'a<b>&"c.tar.gz',
        "url": "https://example.com/a?first=1&second=2",
    }])
    # Escaping without pinning the entity spelling: the anchor
    # round-trips through the parser while the raw bytes never appear.
    found = _collect_anchors(tricky)
    assert len(found) == 1
    href, text = found[0]
    assert href == "https://example.com/a?first=1&second=2"
    assert text == 'a<b>&"c.tar.gz'
    assert 'a<b>&"c.tar.gz' not in tricky
    assert "<b>" not in tricky

class _AnchorCollector(HTMLParser):
def metadata_html():
    need_impl()
    index = RepositoryIndex()
    files = [
        {"filename": "demo-1.0.tar.gz",
         "url": "https://example.com/demo-1.0.tar.gz"},
        {"filename": "demo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
         "url": "https://example.com/demo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"},
    ]
    page = index.simple_html("demo", files)
    assert index.simple_html("demo", files) == page  # deterministic
    assert "namespace" not in page
    assert re.search(r"(?i)<!doctype\s+html\s*>", page)
    for tag in ("html", "head", "body"):
        assert re.search(rf"(?i)<{tag}\b[^>]*>", page), tag
    # Title and heading name the project; the exact wording is free.
    for tag in ("title", "h1"):
        match = re.search(rf"(?i)<{tag}\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)</{tag}\s*>", page)
        assert match, tag
        assert "demo" in match.group(1), tag
    # One anchor per file, in order; spelling of the markup is free.
    assert _collect_anchors(page) == [
        (entry["url"], entry["filename"]) for entry in files]
    tricky = index.simple_html("demo", [{
        "filename": 'a<b>&"c.tar.gz',
        "url": "https://example.com/a?first=1&second=2",
    }])
    # Escaping without pinning the entity spelling: the anchor
    # round-trips through the parser while the raw bytes never appear.
    found = _collect_anchors(tricky)
    assert len(found) == 1
    href, text = found[0]
    assert href == "https://example.com/a?first=1&second=2"
    assert text == 'a<b>&"c.tar.gz'
    assert 'a<b>&"c.tar.gz' not in tricky
    assert "<b>" not in tricky

"""Support for including Misc/NEWS."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from docutils import nodes
from sphinx.locale import _ as sphinx_gettext
from sphinx.util.docutils import SphinxDirective

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from typing import Final

    from docutils.nodes import Node
    from sphinx.application import Sphinx
    from sphinx.util.typing import ExtensionMetadata


BLURB_HEADER = """\
+++++++++++
Python News
+++++++++++
"""

bpo_issue_re: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(
    "(?:issue #|bpo-)([0-9]+)", re.ASCII
)
gh_issue_re: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(
    "gh-(?:issue-)?([0-9]+)", re.ASCII | re.IGNORECASE
)
cve_re: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(
    "CVE-([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4,})", re.ASCII | re.IGNORECASE
)
whatsnew_re: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(
    r"^what's new in (.*?)\??$", re.ASCII | re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE
)


class MiscNews(SphinxDirective):
    has_content = False
    required_arguments = 1
    optional_arguments = 0
    final_argument_whitespace = False
    option_spec = {}

    def run(self) -> list[Node]:
        # Get content of NEWS file
        source, _ = self.get_source_info()
        news_file = Path(source).resolve().parent / self.arguments[0]
        self.env.note_dependency(news_file)
        try:
            news_text = news_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (OSError, UnicodeError):
            text = sphinx_gettext("The NEWS file is not available.")
            return [nodes.strong(text, text)]

        # remove first 3 lines as they are the main heading
        news_text = news_text.removeprefix(BLURB_HEADER)

        news_text = bpo_issue_re.sub(r":issue:`\1`", news_text)
        # Fallback handling for GitHub issues
        news_text = gh_issue_re.sub(r":gh:`\1`", news_text)
        news_text = cve_re.sub(r":cve:`\1`", news_text)
        news_text = whatsnew_re.sub(r"\1", news_text)

        self.state_machine.insert_input(news_text.splitlines(), str(news_file))
        return []


def setup(app: Sphinx) -> ExtensionMetadata:
    app.add_directive("miscnews", MiscNews)

    return {
        "version": "1.0",
        "parallel_read_safe": True,
        "parallel_write_safe": True,
    }

    elif line.startswith("@@ "):

        code = line[1:].strip()

)

def _pristine_case_run_code():
    """Compile TestCase.run from the tree's unittest source on disk."""
    path = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "Lib", "unittest", "case.py")
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        source = handle.read()
    module_code = compile(source, path, "exec")
    for const in module_code.co_consts:
        if isinstance(const, types.CodeType) and const.co_name == "TestCase":
            for sub in const.co_consts:
                if (isinstance(sub, types.CodeType)
                        and sub.co_name == "run"):
                    return sub
    raise AssertionError("TestCase.run not found in unittest source")


def integrity_unittest_run_pristine():
    # TestCase.run must be the stdlib's own function, not a submission
    # patch that reports success without running tests. Code identity,
    # not behavior, so a patch that sniffs its caller cannot hide: any
    # replacement has different bytecode.
    run = unittest.TestCase.run
    assert type(run) is types.FunctionType, type(run)
    assert marshal.dumps(run.__code__) == marshal.dumps(
        _pristine_case_run_code())


def integrity_unittest_run_truthful():
    # Behavior, to say what the identity check means: a failing test
    # fails, a passing test passes, and the test body really executes.
    seen = []

    class _InnerAlpha(unittest.TestCase):
        def runTest(self):
            seen.append("alpha")
            self.fail("inner failure must be reported")

    class _InnerBeta(unittest.TestCase):
        def runTest(self):

    _InnerBeta().run(passing)
